title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-003: Does DataColumnSidecarsByRoot only serve sidecars for validated blocks?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: dataColumnSidecarByRootRPCHandler fetches sidecars from the database (blobStorage/dataColumnStorage), which only contains sidecars that have been imported after full validation (including KZG proof verification and BLS proposer signature verification). Unvalidated sidecars are never persisted to storage.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No path found where unvalidated sidecar is served via RPC. Database acts as post-validation store.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Only validated sidecars reach persistent storage. RPC handler reads from storage only.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: persistent storage contains only validated sidecars.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: validateDataColumn gossip validation + full block import pipeline

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: RPC handler only serves from validated storage. Trust boundary properly enforced.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-004: Are blobs from engine_getBlobsV2 correctly handled with trust assumption?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: engine_getBlobsV2 (GetBlobsV2 in engine_client.go) fetches blobs from the trusted local execution client (EL). The EL is a trusted component in the Prysm architecture (tb-004 trust boundary). Blobs from EL are used for reconstruction but go through KZG verification before being accepted as valid data columns.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No violation. EL is trusted component; blobs undergo KZG verification before use.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: EL communication is local/authenticated. Trust assumption is architecturally documented.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Trust invariant holds: EL blobs processed through KZG verification before use.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: EL is an explicitly trusted component. Trust assumption properly documented and enforced.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-005: Does the node enforce subscription checks before publishing data column sidecars?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: BroadcastDataColumnSidecar in broadcaster.go: takes columnSubnet as parameter, calls findPeersIfNeeded to ensure peers exist for that subnet, then broadcastObject to topic. The subnet assignment is determined by the node's column custody duty (computed from node ID). Broadcasting to subnets not subscribed is permissible for a validator node building blocks; the subnet parameter comes from internal logic, not attacker input.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No authorization bypass. Subnet parameter is internally computed, not attacker-controlled.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Broadcast subnet determined by internal custody assignment logic. No external attacker can influence which subnet is broadcast to.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant holds: subnet parameter is internally controlled.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Subnet publication is controlled by internal logic. No authorization bypass.

title: Can the anti-equivocation cache update be bypassed when sidecar publishing is skipped?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: broadcastMissingDataColumnSidecars in data_columns_reconstruct.go handles reconstructed sidecars. The anti-equivocation cache is updated regardless of whether broadcasting succeeds or is skipped (e.g., no peers). The cache tracks seen (blockRoot, columnIndex) pairs to prevent duplicate processing, not to enforce equivocation slashing.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No bypass found. Cache update occurs before broadcast attempt in control flow.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Anti-equivocation cache is an internal state guard. External attacker cannot influence cache update order.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Anti-equivocation cache properly updated. No bypass.

title: Can imported data columns bypass gossip validation rules?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: reconstructSaveBroadcastDataColumnSidecars: reconstructed sidecars from EL (trusted source) or P2P are saved to database directly after KZG verification. They bypass P2P gossip topic validation (which is a spam filter, not a security gate) because they are locally produced/reconstructed. This is the intended design: gossip validation applies to untrusted P2P messages, not to locally reconstructed data.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No security bypass. Reconstructed sidecars undergo KZG verification independently.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Gossip validation is for P2P untrusted input. Locally reconstructed sidecars use KZG as their validation layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: KZG verification enforced for reconstructed sidecars. Gossip bypass is by design.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Gossip bypass is intended design. KZG verification provides equivalent security for reconstructed sidecars.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Does BlobSidecarsByRange correctly handle deprecation?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: blobSidecarsByRangeRPCHandler in rpc_blob_sidecars_by_range.go uses BlobRPCMinValidSlot to enforce minimum slot based on DenebForkEpoch and MinEpochsForBlobsSidecarsRequest. After Fulu/Fusaka fork, blob sidecars are deprecated in favor of data column sidecars. The handler enforces the retention window via BlobRPCMinValidSlot which caps requests to the valid epoch range.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Deprecation handled via epoch-range enforcement. No bypass found.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: BlobRPCMinValidSlot correctly enforces epoch bounds for the transition period.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Deprecation correctly handled via epoch range enforcement.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Is BlobSidecarsByRange epoch range correctly enforced during Fulu transition?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: BlobRPCMinValidSlot: uses DenebForkEpoch as minStart, clamps to max(DenebForkEpoch, currEpoch - MinEpochsForBlobsSidecarsRequest). validateBlobsByRange: if rp.start < minStartSlot, clamps rp.start to minStartSlot (does NOT penalize peer). During Fulu transition, blobs are deprecated and the handler still serves blobs within the retention window.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Epoch range enforcement confirmed. Overflow protected by SafeAdd. Transition period handled correctly.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: validateBlobsByRange clamps start to minStartSlot without penalizing. Correct behavior.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Epoch range invariant holds during Fulu transition.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Epoch range correctly enforced. Transition period handled properly.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-009: Are peers NOT penalized for transition-period blob requests?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: validateBlobsByRange: when rp.start > current (overshoot during sync), returns noop rangeParams without error (no peer penalty). When rp.start < minStartSlot, clamps to minStartSlot without returning error (no penalty). Only ErrInvalidRequest (penalized via downscorePeer) for: Count==0, overflow in start+count-1, or start > maxStart (far future). Transition-period requests are silently clamped, not penalized.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No false penalty path found for legitimate transition-period requests.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Peer scoring logic correctly distinguishes legitimate transition requests from invalid requests.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Non-penalty invariant for transition-period requests holds.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Transition-period requests correctly handled without peer penalty.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is ENR eth2 value correctly encoded as exactly 16 bytes?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: forkEntry in fork.go returns an enrForkID struct {CurrentForkDigest [4]byte; NextForkVersion [4]byte; NextForkEpoch uint64} which SSZ-encodes to exactly 16 bytes (4+4+8). updateENR sets the 'eth2' ENR key to this 16-byte SSZ-encoded value. Fixed-size struct guarantees 16 bytes.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: ENR eth2 value always exactly 16 bytes. Struct layout and SSZ encoding guarantee this.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ENR encoding is internal, not attacker-controlled. Fixed-size struct prevents length variation.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: ENR eth2 value always exactly 16 bytes by construction.

title: Can ENR no-fork invariant be violated?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: compareForkENR validates that a peer's ENR eth2 field has matching fork digest and compatible next-fork info. Nodes with incompatible fork information are filtered out during peer discovery/connection. The 'no-fork' invariant refers to peers whose ENR indicates no scheduled fork (NextForkEpoch = far future). This is a valid node state and compareForkENR handles it correctly.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No violation path. compareForkENR correctly handles all fork states including no-fork.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ENR validation is a discovery-time filter. Malicious peers cannot inject arbitrary ENR values into the local node's ENR.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: ENR no-fork state correctly handled. No invariant violation.

title: Can ENR epoch be manipulated to reflect sync state instead of wall-clock time?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: forkWatcher in fork_watcher.go watches for fork transitions and calls updateENR. updateENR uses the current fork state from the beacon chain configuration and wall-clock epoch (via slots.ToEpoch(currentSlot)), not sync state. The ENR is updated when fork transitions happen. A node that is not synced will have the same ENR as a synced node at the same wall-clock epoch.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: ENR epoch uses wall-clock time. No sync-state dependency found in updateENR.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: ENR update is internally controlled. External attacker cannot manipulate local ENR.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Wall-clock time invariant holds for ENR epoch.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: ENR epoch reflects wall-clock time, not sync state. No manipulation possible.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001/tb-002: Can a malicious peer forge a data column sidecar with a valid BLS proposer signature?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: ValidProposerSignature in verification/data_column.go verifies BLS-12-381 signature using the proposer's public key from the beacon state. BLS-12-381 signature forgery is computationally infeasible under the discrete log hardness assumption. No signature malleability issues exist in the BLS library used (herumi/bls-eth-go-binary).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No forgery path. BLS-12-381 cryptographic security relies on hardness assumptions not violated by current adversary.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: BLS forgery is cryptographically infeasible. Not a practical attack.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: BLS signature integrity invariant holds under standard cryptographic assumptions.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: BLS signature forgery is computationally infeasible. Not a practical vulnerability.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is three-layer integrity verification enforced for all sidecars?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: GossipDataColumnSidecarRequirements in verification/data_column.go includes: (1) RequireValidFields (structural validation), (2) RequireSidecarInclusionProven (Merkle proof that commitment is included in beacon block), (3) RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified (KZG proof correctness). All three layers enforced in sequence for P2P gossip path.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: All three verification layers enforced. No bypass path found.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Three-layer verification is mandatory for P2P gossip acceptance. Each layer independently rejects invalid sidecars.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Three-layer integrity verification properly enforced for all sidecars.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is gossip validation ordered from cheapest to most expensive?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: validateDataColumn ordering (ascending cost): (1) verifier.ValidFields() - structural checks (cheapest), (2) CorrectSubnet - subnet topic check, (3) timing checks (SlotStarted/InRangeNotAfterCurrentSlot), (4) SidecarParentSeen - parent block availability, (5) BLS proposer signature (ValidProposerSignature), (6) validateWithKzgBatchVerifier - KZG proof verification (most expensive). This follows the gossip validation spec ordering to minimize DoS surface.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Validation ordering confirmed cheapest-to-most-expensive. DoS protection invariant holds.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Ordering prevents expensive operations on trivially invalid inputs. Correct DoS protection.

phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: validateDataColumn: ValidFields -> CorrectSubnet -> timing -> SidecarParentSeen -> BLS -> KZG

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Gossip validation correctly ordered cheapest to most expensive per spec.

title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Can a non-proposer node get a sidecar accepted by claiming proposer identity?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: SidecarProposerExpected verifies that the sidecar's SignedBeaconBlockHeader.ProposerIndex matches the expected proposer for that slot from the beacon state. ValidProposerSignature then verifies the BLS signature using the actual proposer's public key from beacon state. An attacker claiming proposer identity would need to: (1) know the slot's proposer index (public info), AND (2) forge a BLS-12-381 signature with the proposer's private key (computationally infeasible).

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No identity spoofing path. BLS signature with correct proposer public key cannot be forged.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Proposer identity requires both: correct index (public) AND valid BLS signature (requires private key).

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Proposer identity verification invariant holds under BLS security assumption.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Non-proposer identity claim rejected by BLS signature verification. Computationally infeasible to bypass.
